note: Execution-backend flexibility (NOT 'X should be a cloud function'). A CapabilityTask is contract-stable; the execution backend is interchangeable behind ExecutionProviderPort and chosen by policy/telemetry/pricing. Kubernetes, cloud functions, local subprocesses, jobs, pools, and the local emulator can run SIDE BY SIDE and be switched as cost/latency/reliability/cold-start/customer-requirements change. 'eligible' = function-eligible / k8s-eligible by default; choices are reversible policy decisions, overridable WITH PROOF. The DB FleetLedger remains the source of truth; no backend owns truth.
cloud_agnostic_note: AWS Lambda is NOT canonical — it is one peer in the serverless-function FAMILY. All serverless providers are interchangeable behind ExecutionProviderPort and selected by policy/pricebook/health; the local_function_emulator is the required offline equivalent for every one of them. To add a new serverless provider, edit `generic_cloud_functions` + `candidate_local_equivalents` here (config), not the selector code.

compute_ownership.note: WHOSE infra runs the worker — orthogonal to WHICH backend. The easiest onboarding is BYO-via-API-key: a customer supplies a token (e.g. a Cloudflare API token) and workers spin up on THEIR account. Zero infra for us; data-residency for them (their data never leaves their account -> the `locality` descent axis); their compute bill. The DurableFleetLedger + receipts stay OUR truth (we dispatch + record; they execute). Credentials are tenant-scoped SecretRefs (service_auth_consumption_model), never logged.

modes.provider_operated: we run the backend on our own infra/accounts (default).
modes.customer_account: BYO via a customer-supplied API key/token (SecretRef) — we provision/dispatch onto the customer's account (cloudflare_workers, aws_lambda, gcp_cloud_run_function, ...). Easiest start: paste a key.
modes.customer_managed: the customer runs the cluster/endpoint themselves (their k8s / openfaas); we dispatch to their endpoint URL + token.

compute_ownership.onboarding: customer supplies a SecretRef (e.g. secret://tenant/<id>/cloudflare_api_token [+ account_id]); Teleon selects a BYO provider for that tenant by policy; the local_function_emulator stays the offline equivalent so dev never needs a customer key.
invariants: FleetLedger + receipts remain OUR truth even when compute runs on the customer's account
the customer API key is a tenant SecretRef, never logged, never global
a BYO provider never owns truth (owns_truth=false) — it only RUNS the task

_defer_gate: A real cloud/K8s/Docker backend may be CANDIDATE only if it declares a local_emulator_provider below that is built + proven. Cloud can wait; capability cannot. Enforced by check_real_execution_candidates_have_emulators + check_no_deferred_execution_surfaces.

utility.notes: short deterministic tasks; cloud functions MAY be cost-effective; k8s still allowed by volume/packaging

memory_context.notes: small memory writes/recalls MAY fit functions; tenant/project scoping required

ingestion_sync.notes: webhooks/small sources MAY fit functions; large backfills use jobs/pools

verification_fact_check.notes: deterministic verifiers MAY fit functions; reconciliation authority stays separate

browser.notes: browser cold-start + deps are heavy; generic functions allowed ONLY with explicit proof

model_inference.notes: model load + GPU favor pools/jobs; generic functions excluded by default

open_ended_agent.notes: long-running, sandboxed, tool-heavy; generic function only if very small/bounded + proven

parser_document.notes: OCR/parse can be heavy; jobs/pools for large docs

reconciliation_policy.notes: policy decisions + receipts; no LLM truth

control_plane.notes: always-on lightweight supervisor; not a function
